physical.mounting-hardware: M6*15mm Screw x4 and M6 Nut x4

configs.description: The finger duct as FS ships #29038, cover fitted.
configs.name: base

gaps.note: the datasheet calls the cover hinged and detachable; no view draws a hinge, and the cover is drawn as one fitted plate.
gaps.wanted: a drawing or a close render of the cover's end
no bays and no grouped ports to correlate against, so there is nothing to wire yet - group the ports first - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

attrs.note: datasheet - material, colour, the mounting hardware, the two pass-through holes, the detachable cover and the 2.87 in finger duct are the specification table of the finger duct datasheet; RoHS and ISO 9001 are its Standards Compliance list.

base.note: drawing - the base behind the ear plane reads 440.7 wide on the top view, 3.9 mm wider each side than the duct it carries; it is drawn the width of the duct, the body between the ear folds.

bottom.note: drawing - the front view draws the same finger tips along the bottom as along the top, and the side view draws two equal walls; the bottom is the top again.

capacity.note: datasheet - the Cable Capacity Reference Guide table of the same datasheet gives CMH-SFD1U per cable type at 30 per cent and 100 per cent fill, and notes that the copper figures are theoretical, for reference only, with 30 per cent the recommended fill and 100 per cent the maximum. The figure stated is the Cat6 24AWG 6.1 mm row, the cable the FHD-CMP5DR datasheet states its own capacity in. Not divided among the slots: FS states it for the manager.

chassis.note: drawing - THE BODY BETWEEN THE EARS, as every rack device in the library is modelled. The datasheet gives 44 x 482.6 x 87 mm (1.73 x 19 x 3.43 in) overall. The ears are the ends of the moulded base plate, 44 high, with a slot, a round hole and a slot each; they are not drawn, and they take 24.8 mm at each end. The duct between them reads 431.6 on the front view, 433.4 on the top view and 434.2 on the straight-on render, and 433.0 is taken. Its 42 is the side view, across the two finger walls. `depth` STATES THE VENDOR OVERALL 87, AND IT IS NOT ALL ON ONE SIDE OF THE RAIL: the base stands 11.3 mm behind the plane of the ears, the fingers 60 mm in front of it, and the cover clips on over their tips. The rear view is the back of the base; the front view is the cover.

color.note: estimated - "Color: Black". Every image FS publishes of the part is a render; their medians read 37 to 40 on each channel on the base and 45 on the cover, so the cover is drawn a shade lighter than the duct.

front.note: drawing - the cover, fitted. The front view of the datasheet draws the duct with the cover off - the two rows of finger tips end-on, the channel between them and the pass-through holes at the back of it. The `duct` guide is the 25 mm between the inner faces of the finger walls on that view, dimensioned 0.98 in [25mm], over the full width of the duct.

full-depth.note: `full-depth: false` - the fingers stand 60 mm in front of the mounting plane and the base only 11.3 behind it (the vendor's side view), so the rear face of its rack unit stays free for another part (#854).

guides.note: drawing - the duct on the front view is the channel between the finger walls, run across the rack; finger pitch and gap are the top view figures above.

left.note: drawing - the side view of CMH-SFD1U, 2.45 px/mm across its 42: the base, the two finger walls 7.3 thick with 25 between them, and the hooked tips the cover clips to, drawn as the cover lips over them. The duct is open at both ends, and a cable runs out of it there: nothing is built across the ends.

method.note: FIGURES FROM THE VENDOR DRAWING. FS publishes one datasheet for CMH-SFD1U, CMH-SFD2U and CMH-DFD1U (Horizontal Cable Managers with Finger Duct), with a front view and a top and side view of each part, inch dimensions with millimetres in brackets. The front view is 2.671 px/mm across the 482.6 and 2.68 down the 44; the top view 2.192 across and 2.207 down the 87, 0.7 per cent apart: both are orthographic and carry geometry to about half a millimetre. The renders of #29038 on the FS product page are the second reading, and one of them is a straight-on plan.

rear.note: drawing - the back of the base with the two pass-through holes, from the front view of the datasheet, which draws them through the channel: 76.4 wide (3.03 in [77mm]), 25 high, 171.2 apart (6.74 in), 325.2 over both (12.8 in), symmetric about the middle. The render of the back confirms two holes, the fingers seen through them, and a round boss in the middle. The back is built as five plates round the two holes, sunk 0.05 inside the rear face so the base closes between the well floor and the back within the 87 mm envelope, and each hole goes through into the channel. (0.1.1 built them 11.3 OUTWARD, 98.3 deep overall with a gap behind the floor.)

rear-not-drawn.note: drawing - the boss in the middle of the base and the moulded recycling and material marks at its left end in the render of the back are not drawn: the boss reads as a vendor mark, and a mark is never drawn. The ribs on the back of the base are not drawn.

shell.note: drawing - A HOLLOW DUCT, NOT A BOX. Cables lie in the channel between the two rows of fingers, so the body is a sheet body (docs/cable-managers-design.md section 4) and its six views are elevations. The solid is what its parts build: the base plate on the front view as a well 75.5 deep, whose floor is open at the two pass-through holes; the two rows of fingers standing in it, each with its share of the root of the wall; the cover in it across the finger tips, which lifts off and opens the channel; and the back of the base standing 11.3 proud of the rear face. The channel and its two ends are open air.

thickness.note: estimated - no FS document states a wall gauge for the ABS moulding. 7.3 is the finger wall read off the side view of the datasheet at 2.45 px/mm, 18 px; the base and the cover are thinner or thicker, each in its own part.

top.note: drawing - the top view, rear at y=0: the base 11.3 deep behind the ear plane, then the finger wall, then the cover from 72 to the front. Twelve slots: their centres run 74.77 px apart over eleven pitches, 34.1 mm, where the dimension line prints 1.32 in [33.6mm]; over eleven pitches that is 5.5 mm, twelve pixels, and the front view agrees with the drawing at 91.3 px, 34.2 mm, so the pitch is the drawing and the label is not taken. The gap prints 0.63 in [16mm] and measures 16.4 between the centres of its outlines, so 16.0 is taken. Each slot is round at its root, 22.2 from the rear, and narrows to a 4 mm neck under the cover - the flared tips of the fingers that hold a cable in. The slot depth reads 47.8 against the dimensioned 46.6 from the neck. The finger in the middle is centred on the duct, on both views and in the straight-on render, whose twelve openings agree.
